People in India are switching to UPI because paying becomes as easy as sending a message, and it costs the user nothing.

Launched by NPCI in 2016, UPI links your bank account to a phone app, so money moves straight from one account to another in seconds. There's no cash to carry, no waiting for change and no card details to hand over. A street vendor selling ₹10 tea can take payment the same way a big shop does, with just a printed QR code.

The three main reasons:

Free and instant: Most everyday payments carry no fee, and money arrives in seconds, at any hour, even on holidays.
Works everywhere: One QR code or phone number works across every bank and payment app, from small stalls to large stores.
Simple and safe enough: A PIN confirms each payment, and you never share your card or account number with the shop.

Cheap smartphones and mobile data helped too. Once most people around you pay this way, it becomes the easy default, and cash starts to feel like the slow option.
